title: Purify and Generalize: Efficient Dual-End Adapters for Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Sequential recommendation is challenged by noisy interactions that corrupt input representations and by sharp-minimum overfitting to popularity patterns, causing unstable predictions and poor generalization.

gap.claim: Existing mitigations often require model-specific modifications and rely on uniform transformations without adaptive control or instance-aware mechanisms.

contributions.claim: DEASRec is a lightweight dual-end adapter that plugs into sequential-recommendation backbones without modifying their architectures.
PVM performs subspace-adaptive bounded modulation in polar complex space to decouple magnitude and phase for input-noise filtering.
ASR injects instance-aware Gaussian perturbations during training to encourage convergence toward flat minima.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present DEASRec as a novel Dual-End Adapter for Sequential Recommendation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On four real-world datasets, the authors report that DEASRec integrates with different backbone architectures and yields stable performance improvements at low computational cost.
The authors report competitive performance against state-of-the-art baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommendation faces input noise and output overfitting.
Existing approaches lack adaptive, instance-aware control and commonly require model-specific changes.
DEASRec introduces input-end PVM and output-end ASR as lightweight adapters.
PVM purifies noisy inputs while ASR promotes flatter minima, forming a purify-then-generalize pipeline.
Experiments report integration across backbones, stable improvements, low computational cost, and competitive baseline performance.

source_observation.claim: The method separates input purification from output-side generalization using distinct lightweight adapters.

interpretation.claim: Different failure modes in a sequential model may benefit from interventions at different processing ends.

application.claim: When adapting an existing backbone, consider modular interventions that target input corruption and optimization overfitting separately.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this separation is necessary across tasks, datasets, or backbone types.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four datasets, evaluation metrics, or quantitative improvement magnitudes.
The abstract does not provide details of the theoretical grounding, perturbation settings, or computational-cost measurements.
The abstract does not identify the compared state-of-the-art baselines.
